chunks: And by his chain, he said:

‘Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: ‘I do not sow the crop to seek surplus/profit in it, and I do not sow it except so that the beggar may take from it, and the one with need, and the grouse may take from it, particularly among the birds.’

key_terms.الْمُعْتَرُّ: the beggar / one who asks for charity
key_terms.ذُو الْحَاجَةِ: the one with need / the needy

ai.seo_question: What was Imam Sajid's intention when farming his land?
ai.summary: Imam ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) illustrates the Shia ideal of *sadaqah* (charity) by framing agriculture not as a commercial enterprise for wealth accumulation, but as a means of distributing sustenance to the needy and even animals. This narration highlights the spiritual merit of intentional generosity, where the farmer’s primary goal is the benefit of others, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of stewardship over resources for the common good.

en.hubeali: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘I do not farm the plantation in order to seek the Grace in it, and I<sup>asws</sup> do not farm except for the beggar to take from it, and the one with the need, and what the grouse takes from it, particularly from the birds’.
en.sarwar: 2. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith

the following is narrated: “Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘I do not work in plantation for gains except that I want this gain for the destitute, the needy and especially for the lark among birds/”
